Chat threads as terminals

Features·seedling·proposed·JUL 21, 2026

Architectural wire: Xyne Spaces ↔ pesu ↔ padi/kaval — one thread per terminal, messages only. Build the conversation face in kolu first; pesu reuses it.

One conversation ↔ one kolu terminal. User text → terminal input; agent messages (not tools/edits) → conversation. The chat surface can be the kolu UI first, then Xyne Spaces via pesu — same pipe, different face.

pesu is the XS bridge only; config is env/systemd next to pesu, not the web app.

Components

Three processes on the chat side of the wall; four on the machine side. The browser PWA is not on the critical path — same class of client as padi-tui / kolu mcp.

Component Process Job in this design
Xyne Spaces XS cloud Threads, identity, @mention/DM delivery, message store
XS apps platform part of XS Signed webhook out; app API in (postMessage, updateMessage, user/info)
pesu new daemon beside kolu (packages/pesu) HTTP webhook receiver + bind store + padi client + XS API client
padi workspace daemon padiSurface: lifecycle.create, lifecycle.sendInput, awareness, transcript load
kaval PTY daemon under padi Owns the live PTY; serializes writes
agent CLI child in the PTY claude / codex / opencode / grok — writes its own session files
transcript loaders in-process in padi today Vendor file → transcript-core IR (user · assistant · tool_* · …)
kolu PWA browser Depth only: open the bound terminal via deep link 
Xyne Spaces ──HTTPS──► pesu ──unix socket──► padi ──unix socket──► kaval ──PTY──► agent
     ▲                   │                      │
     │                   │                      └── loaders ← session files on disk
     └──── HTTPS API ────┘

pesu dials padi with the same kit as other non-browser faces (@kolu/padi/dial → digest-keyed socket, control-core handshake, contract skew fail-fast). It does not go through kolu-server.

Bind state (pesu-local)

pesu holds the only new durable fact:

threadId  →  { terminalId, authorUserId, hostKey? }
  • Create on miss — first webhook for an unbound thread runs lifecycle.create (+ agent launch), then stores the row.
  • Author gate — later webhooks must match authorUserId (v1: one allowlisted operator). Mismatch → visible decline via postMessage, never silence, never sendInput.
  • Not in kolu’s conf store; not in XS. Survives pesu restart if persisted next to pesu (file/env scope TBD; start with on-disk JSON beside the daemon).

Interaction: first message

End-to-end create + first prompt.

Step From → to What moves
1 User → XS DM or @bot text in a channel
2 XS → pesu POST webhook: APP_MENTIONED or DIRECT_MESSAGE. Payload: conversationId, userId, cleanContent, messageId. Header: X-Xyne-Signature (HMAC of raw body)
3 pesu Verify HMAC (constant-time) → 200 immediately → work async (XS does not retry)
4 pesu → XS optional user/info to resolve display name; cache
5 pesu → padi lifecycle.create({ cwd? }) → { id: terminalId }
6 padi → kaval spawn PTY (shell)
7 pesu → padi lifecycle.sendInput({ id, data: "<agent argv>\\r" }) — same initial-command path as padi-tui create -- claude …
8 pesu → padi lifecycle.sendInput({ id, data: "<user text>\\r" }) — first agent prompt
9 pesu persist bind conversationId → { terminalId, authorUserId }
10 pesu → XS postMessage into conversationId: ack + deep link to open that terminal in kolu

Agent is unaware of chat. It only sees PTY input.

Interaction: later user messages

Step From → to What moves
1 XS → pesu same webhook shape
2 pesu lookup bind by conversationId; reject if author ≠ stored
3 pesu → padi lifecycle.sendInput({ id: terminalId, data: "<text>\\r" })
4 kaval write bytes into that PTY (last-writer-wins at kaval)

No second terminal. No coordinator hop. Thread is the mailbox for one PTY.

Interaction: agent → thread (transcript path)

This is the return half. Today kolu can load a full transcript; it does not yet stream assistant events to a third party.

Step Component What
A agent CLI appends to vendor session store (Claude JSONL, Codex/OpenCode SQLite, …)
B padi sensors already watch those files for agent state (working / waiting / awaiting_user) — not for chat text
C loaders loadClaudeCodeTranscript / loadCodexTranscript / … → Transcript IR
D filter keep kind === "assistant" only (same cut as HTML chat log mode — drop tool_call, tool_result, reasoning, edits)
E pesu → XS postMessage / updateMessage with that text into the bound thread

Gap: C–E need a live feed. Options, in order of honesty:

  1. New padi stream — e.g. transcript.events({ id }) yields snapshot-then-deltas of IR events (or chat-filtered). pesu subscribes over the same socket. Preferred: one source of truth, reconnectable like other surface streams.
  2. Poll loaders — pesu re-loads transcript on a short interval, diffs assistant texts, posts new ones. Coarser; no padi API change; fine for a first slice.

Until one of those exists, the outbound half is incomplete; inbound (create + sendInput) can still ship alone.

What each API is (and is not)

Xyne Spaces → pesu (webhook)

Event When
APP_MENTIONED explicit @bot in a channel
DIRECT_MESSAGE every message in the bot DM

Plain channel messages without @ are not delivered to installed apps. pesu answers 200 first; failures after that are pesu’s problem (post a visible error into the thread).

pesu → Xyne Spaces (app API, bearer JWT)

Call Use
POST …/chat/postMessage new bot turn (or first ack)
POST …/chat/updateMessage grow one message while an assistant turn streams
POST …/chat/agentProgress optional typing indicator during a turn
GET …/user/info resolve sender id → name

pesu → padi (padiSurface over unix socket)

Procedure Use
lifecycle.create new terminal (optional cwd)
lifecycle.sendInput agent launch line + every user message
(future) transcript stream or export assistant text out

pesu does not call kaval directly. padi owns the terminal id space and awareness; kaval is an implementation detail behind lifecycle.*.

Out of scope for this wire

  • Fleet board / who-needs-me in chat
  • Coordinator multi-worker campaigns
  • Routing chat traffic through kolu-server or the PWA
  • Bot secrets in the web UI

pesu internal shape

packages/pesu/
  bin.ts          # listen + dial padi + load binds
  webhook.ts      # HMAC verify, parse, 200, enqueue
  xyneApi.ts      # postMessage · updateMessage · user/info
  binds.ts        # threadId → terminalId (+ author)
  turns.ts        # create-on-miss · author gate · sendInput
  mirror.ts       # assistant events → postMessage (stream or poll)
  config.ts       # XS base URL, secrets via env, agent argv, cwd, allowlist

Same layering idea as padi-tui: thin composition over existing padi verbs; no second terminal protocol.

Build order — not pesu first

Full pesu needs XS credentials, webhooks, and a public URL. The interesting half of the product does not: a conversation face on one terminal, using transcript messages + sendInput. That is useful in kolu alone — and it is what /bridge does by hand via MCP (sendInput, wait for agent state, read output), but as a real UI instead of a skill loop.

Do first Why
CT1 + CH1 De-risk the message pipe; ship a nifty kolu feature with no XS
PE0 Chat can create/drive a terminal from XS (half duplex is still useful)
PE1 Reuse CT1’s chat filter; XS becomes another consumer of the same path

Not in this tree: multi-agent campaign board / bridge dashboard as product UI — that is a different note (campaign surface). Here we only productize the 1:1 conversation that pesu will also use.

CT1 — chat transcript as data

CT1· padi: structured chat events, not only HTML export▶ do next

Today: transcript.exportHtml returns a document. Loaders already build a vendor-neutral IR (user · assistant · tool_* · …).

Ship: a padi procedure (name TBD, e.g. transcript.chat / transcript.get) that returns the chat-filtered event list for a live terminal — same cut as HTML chat-log mode. Consumers: kolu UI, MCP, later pesu.

Optional follow-on inside CT1 if poll is painful: stream transcript.events({ id }) snapshot-then-deltas (surface stream invariants). Poll of the procedure is enough to start CH1.

Done when: client or MCP can fetch assistant/user messages for a terminal without rendering HTML.

CH1 — conversation face in kolu

CH1· UI: chat pane on one terminal — like driving via /bridge, but product○ todo
needs ← CT1

What you get: for the focused agent terminal, a conversation view — bubbles from CT1 (assistant in, your prompts as user), compose box that calls lifecycle.sendInput. Toggle or split with the raw PTY (depth still there). No tools, no edit spam — that is the point.

This is the /bridge human loop productized for one terminal: type a message, see the reply, without living in the agent TUI or an MCP skill. Not a multi-worker board.

Done when: you can run a whole agent turn from the chat face on desktop and mobile without opening the export dialog; the PTY still works for depth.

PE0 — pesu inbound

PE0· XS webhook → create terminal + sendInput○ todo
needs ← CH1

What you get: first DM/@mention creates terminal+agent, stores threadId → terminalId, later messages (author only) go in via sendInput. Ack + deep link into kolu. Replies still read in kolu (CH1) until PE1.

Done when: phone → XS → agent is running on your machine; you can continue in kolu’s conversation face.

PE1 — pesu outbound

PE1· assistant events → XS postMessage○ todo
needs ← CT1 · PE0

Subscribe or poll CT1; post new assistant texts into the bound thread. updateMessage / agentProgress optional here or PE2.

Done when: agent replies appear in the XS thread without tools/edits.

PE2 — deep link + turn UX

PE2· open terminal in PWA; growing reply; typing indicator○ todo
needs ← PE0

Polish only — no new architecture. Deep link on create; grow one bot message while a turn streams; agentProgress while working.

Done criterion (full tree)

DM the bot → terminal under padi/kaval → first prompt is yours → assistant replies in the XS thread (messages only) and the same conversation is readable in kolu’s chat face → deep link opens that terminal.
